title: Network blocker signal harmonization and priority lanes for private deployments
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Context: As inbound private/VPC/on‑prem deployment requests scale, Triage is spending excessive time manually classifying network blockers (proxy, firewall, egress restrictions, OS/kernel constraints, upgrade window conflicts, air‑gapped isolation). This ticket defines a harmonized set of signals + priority lanes to automate routing, reduce manual review time, and make customer-facing SLAs predictable.

Goal: Produce a deterministic classifier (rule + light ML) that ingests intake signals and assigns each request to one of three lanes: fast‑track (self‑serve), standard onboarding, engineering‑assist (requires infra/eng intervention). Provide clear evidence and artifact checklist per lane and integrate with Intake UI + onboarding playbook.

Key signals to capture: inbound network probe results (TCP/UDP reachability to required endpoints), presence of outbound proxies (explicit proxy headers, customer-provided proxy doc), NAT/firewall patterns, declared airgap flag, allowed egress CIDRs, reported OS/distribution and kernel, maintenance/upgrade blackout windows, security/compliance controls (KMS/HSM requirements), and previously-recorded customer telemetry (past retries/failure patterns).

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the full automated remediation flow or change deployment orchestration; it focuses on classification, routing, and automating the checklist + communications. The actual engine that performs network changes remains engineering scope (dependent ENG-19120).

Why now: Incidents and onboarding backlogs are delaying revenue recognition for several mid-market customers. Early experiments with heuristic scoring reduced mean triage time by ~22% but had high variance and poor observability. We need standardized signals, thresholds, and an audit trail for decision rationales.
acceptance_criteria: Signal catalog published in Confluence with JSON schema for each probe and required fields
Priority-lane mapping defined: fast-track / standard / engineering-assist with precise threshold rules
Intake UI shows automated lane assignment and top-3 contributing signals for each request
Automated notifications and a checklist link are sent to customers for fast-track and standard lanes
Operational dashboard with counts by lane and time-to-resolution; baseline established for 30d
Escalation flow documented (who to page, SLA timers) for engineering-assist lane
decisions: Hybrid approach: deterministic rule engine first, supplement with a lightweight classifier in Q3 if variance persists
Default to conservative mapping (err on side of engineering-assist) for unknown/missing signals to avoid failed onprem installs
Expose reasons for lane assignment in the console to enable manual override by SE/PM
Do not store raw customer credentials or private keys in the intake; only hashes/artifact pointers
Use a 3‑tier scoring: severity, likelihood-of-failure, remediation-effort to compute lane assignment
